retained_findings: AWS Powertools is the strongest small structural donor: payload-derived idempotency key, separate validation hash, INPROGRESS/COMPLETE state and conditional concurrency fencing. Its exact current develop head also provides a negative result: a missing in-progress expiry check allowed live records to be reclaimed and concurrent duplicate execution before the current fix.
CloudEvents is a thin identity donor: source+id provides replay/dedup identity while occurrence and emitted event remain distinct; event id must not be overloaded as semantic request identity.

Restate is a useful structural donor for invocation identity plus attach/output after uncertainty, but importing its durable runtime/journal would create an architecture-heavy competing execution/state authority and is rejected for WP-105.

The preferred hypothesis is a minimal F2-native semantic request binder using existing RFC8785/JCS method provenance plus SHA-256, separate invocation/attempt identities, append-only EffectJournal transitions and a non-replayable UNKNOWN_POST_DISPATCH state until verification closes the outcome.

generated_contract_candidate.critical_rule: UNKNOWN_POST_DISPATCH => VERIFY/ATTACH/QUERY original attempt; no blind replay unless the destination effect has an independently proven stable idempotency contract.

next_discriminator: A future Trigger-6 E2 claim should map the minimal semantic_request_sha256 + invocation_id + attempt_id + append-only outcome ABI onto exact current F2-WP-105 source and test for overlap with existing F2/EntityOS primitives. No real effects and no external runtime import are justified at E1.
